skill.name: github-workflow-automation
skill.description: Automates GitHub Actions planning, pull request workflows, release coordination, and CI/CD optimization using GitHub CLI and swarm-style task patterns.
skill.summary: Coordinate GitHub Actions, pull requests, releases, and repository workflow improvements with structured automation prompts.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, documentation links, and GitHub Actions examples. No prompt injection text or covert exfiltration intent was found. The real risk is unpinned third-party CI tooling and autonomous workflow operations that can modify repositories or deployments.

remediation.suggestion: Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs and npm packages to reviewed versions. Avoid alpha or latest dependencies in production workflows.

remediation.issue: Automation can modify repositories or deploy changes
remediation.suggestion: Add manual approval gates before self-healing fixes, pull request creation, publishing, and deployment execution.

remediation.issue: Generated outputs are written directly to GitHub Actions output files
remediation.suggestion: Use documented multiline output syntax, validate generated values, and reject unexpected newlines before writing to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.

remediation.issue: Examples may be copied without review
remediation.suggestion: Mark workflow snippets as templates and tell users to review permissions, secrets, and external dependencies before use.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Third-Party CI Tooling
semantic_findings.description: Examples run ruv-swarm and claude-flow from npm and use ruvnet/swarm-action@v1 without immutable pinning. A compromised package or tag could run code in CI.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file repeatedly recommends npx package execution and a version tag action in CI contexts. These are clear supply-chain risk points unless pinned and reviewed.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Repository and Deployment Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill promotes self-healing, smart publishing, and deployment execution flags without showing approval gates. This can let automation change repositories or deployments based on generated decisions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples include auto-fix, auto-execute, create PR, and publish behavior. The surrounding text does not require manual approval before those actions.

semantic_findings.title: GitHub Actions Output Injection Risk
semantic_findings.description: Workflow examples write generated command output directly to $GITHUB_OUTPUT. If values contain newlines or crafted content, downstream outputs or matrices could be changed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples echo tool output directly into GitHub Actions output files. This is a known unsafe pattern when output is not normalized or delimited.

content.value_statement: GitHub workflow work often spreads across Actions files, pull requests, issues, and release tasks. This skill gives structured commands and templates for planning, optimizing, and coordinating those tasks.
actual_capabilities: Generate GitHub Actions workflow examples for CI, security scanning, deployment, and releases.
Suggest optimization patterns for caching, matrices, parallel jobs, and failure analysis.
Coordinate pull request, issue, release, and multi-repository workflows with GitHub CLI examples.
Provide Claude-Flow and ruv-swarm command patterns for swarm-style automation.
Outline secure workflow practices, including secrets, permissions, OIDC, and audit steps.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI, git, Node.js, and related swarm tools to be installed separately.
Examples are templates and must be reviewed before use in production repositories.
Does not verify that referenced npm packages or GitHub Actions are trustworthy.
Automation can modify workflows, issues, pull requests, and deployments if run without guardrails.

use_cases.title: Plan CI/CD Workflows
use_cases.description: Design GitHub Actions workflows for build, test, security scan, artifact, and deployment stages.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Organize labels, checks, comments, reviewer tasks, and merge readiness for active pull requests.

use_cases.title: Review Workflow Risk
use_cases.description: Identify workflow permissions, secret handling, dependency pinning, and approval gates before rollout.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic CI Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GitHub workflow automation skill to design a simple CI workflow for a Node.js repository. Include test, lint, cache, and pull request triggers.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my GitHub Actions workflow and suggest changes for caching, job parallelism, permissions, and failure reporting. Explain each recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Pull Request Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a pull request automation flow for labels, reviewer assignment, checks, security review, and final merge readiness. Include manual approval points.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Repository Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced release coordination plan across three repositories. Include version alignment, changelog generation, dependency updates, rollout stages, and rollback checks.

output_examples.input: Create a basic CI workflow plan for a TypeScript service.
output_examples.output: A staged plan with checkout, dependency cache, install, lint, test, build, artifact upload, and required branch protections.

output_examples.input: Optimize a slow workflow that repeats installation in every job.
output: A matrix plan that limits redundant work.
A list of measurements to confirm savings.

output_examples.input: Plan a release process for a monorepo.
output_examples.output: A release checklist covering changed packages, version selection, changelog review, staged deployment, and post-release monitoring.

best_practices: Review every generated workflow before committing it to a protected branch.
Pin third-party actions and packages to trusted versions or commit SHAs.
Keep deployment, issue creation, and self-healing steps behind explicit approval controls.
anti_patterns: Running generated workflows with broad repository permissions.
Using latest or alpha dependencies in production CI without review.
Allowing automation to create, merge, or deploy changes without human approval.

faq.question: Does this skill run GitHub Actions by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and templates that a user or agent can run after review.

faq.question: Can I use it with private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, if GitHub CLI authentication and repository permissions are configured correctly.

faq.question: Does it require Claude-Flow or ruv-swarm?
faq.answer: Many examples reference those tools, so install and review them before use.

faq.question: Is it safe for production CI?
faq.answer: Use it only after pinning dependencies, limiting permissions, and adding approval gates.

faq.question: Can it help with pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for PR validation, comments, checks, labels, and review coordination.

faq.question: What should I review first?
faq.answer: Check workflow permissions, external actions, npm packages, secrets handling, and deployment commands.
